references.claim: Specification and runtime repository authority are provisionally separated.
Promotion requires exact evidence, independent gates and human authority; missing evidence blocks.
Rollback, revocation and invalidation are documented but recovery proof requires independent verification.
Static bearer identities authorize caller-selected tenant/workspace values against configured membership, including wildcard support.
Artifact routes authenticate structurally and authorize the supplied workspace before scoped domain calls.
Artifact storage has workspace fields and indexes, but no row-level policy or tenant foreign key is declared in this schema.
CI checks out the PR head or event SHA and runs schemas, P0, Prisma generation and quality gates.
Bootstrap identities issue HMAC sessions; credential expiry and revocation are rechecked; client tenant header is checked against principal membership.
Public lead intake validates input, persists lead/evidence/job transactionally and performs notification after commit.
User URL drives HTTP(S) robots, page and sitemap requests with time/size bounds; no private-address or DNS-rebinding enforcement appears in this path.
Assessment and department jobs are drained by in-process polling loops.
Assessment approval names an exact revision and hash and uses authenticated tenant context.
Department approval is tenant/status gated but the route does not require an exact draft revision hash.
Models carry tenant fields and indexes, while this schema declares no Tenant relation or row-level security policy.
Evidence is appended and queried through ordinary Prisma operations; tamper-evident external custody is not implemented here.
Runtime expects database, auth, provider, payment and webhook credentials through environment configuration.
Fastify composes auth, CORS, rate limiting, public intake, operator, approval and optional payment routes plus external integrations.
Live secret custody, deployed values and production topology cannot be proven from example configuration.
